prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its bioactive form, which made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for B010 to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not rest on the opening unanimity, and I do not either. The case is a continuous chain from concept to outcome: proglucagon-derived peptides and the incretin effect, the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) form, human physiology of secretion and action, receptor and intestinotrophic biology, and then agonists with large, independently replicated randomised outcome benefit in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is clear, the concept is original, the evidence is mature, and a three-person basic-science allocation fits the emphasis on discovery. I would keep it a single achievement. A second part would not improve the allocation, and every available second part carries its own unresolved credit problem.
statement.case_against: The attribution risk is real and, as the chair says, should be treated as a precondition and not a footnote. Mojsov's priority against the Habener group for identifying and characterising the bioactive peptide is unverified by any of us, Habener is not among the credited names, and Knudsen is left out by the cap. I still hold that the configuration stands only if a documentary check of the primary papers and dates shows Mojsov's contribution to be distinct and not derivative. If that check fails, this three-name set cannot be defended and the committee would need names that the supplied ballot does not offer. Excluding Knudsen is a consequence of the cap and of the discovery emphasis, not a view that half-life extension was incidental, and the citation must say that the physiology made the drugs possible without implying the drugs are an afterthought.

responses.point: The chair would treat Knudsen as first reserve if the attribution review weakens any of the three names, rather than displace a discoverer now, and doubts that B041 competes with B010 in the same year.
responses.response: I accept Knudsen as first reserve and think that is the right order: the principle that justified the long-acting agonists was established by the physiologists, so she should not displace a discoverer before the check is done. If Mojsov's claim were found derivative, though, I would not simply swap Knudsen into her seat, because that would change the prize from a discovery prize to a drug-development prize and the committee should debate that openly. On B041 I take his point. TNF blockade is mature and cleanly attributed, but it is closer to antibody therapy for a known target than to a new biological axis, and I do not set it against B010 this year. Your chair's question on the Mojsov check is the right gate, and I would accept the original 1980s papers and dates, not later recollection, as the standard.

responses.point: Sandberg says a prize that names the drugs would require reconsidering Knudsen at the cost of Mojsov or Drucker, and that if B010 fails the fallback is unclear because B006 has no first-place support and an incomplete attribution.
responses.response: I agree that wording the citation around the drugs would force the Knudsen question, which is why I word it around the physiology and bioactive form and say the work made therapy possible. I also share his worry about the fallback. B006 has the clearest clinical record outside B010, but its credit problem is the same size as B010's, and Eshhar is missing in every version. Narrowing to June and Sadelain removes Rosenberg's broader adoptive-transfer claim but does not remove that gap. I therefore do not think B006 can rescue the committee if the Mojsov check fails. It is a fallback with a known defect, and we should say so before the vote instead of treating it as equivalent.

responses.point: El-Manira argues that removing Rosenberg does not solve the Eshhar problem, and holds that optogenetics has opened previously intractable questions but is mainly a methodological case with early clinical use.
responses.response: His point on Eshhar is correct and I accept it: my two-person B006 is cleaner on Rosenberg but not safe on the origin of the receptor concept, so I keep it only as an alternative. We agree on B008 being mainly methodological. I would add that the split between the channelrhodopsin discovery and its neuronal deployment means that crediting Deisseroth ahead of Boyden needs a documented basis I have not seen, and the present record does not give it. Neither alternative, in my view, is a reason to add a second part to B010. I would rather have one settled prize than two parts, one of which would carry a contested allocation.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps B006 as first alternative and would not reduce it to two names before the Eshhar question is resolved, and notes that Walter and Mori cover only the Ire1 and HAC1/XBP1 core of B020.
responses.response: I have moved toward his position. Having heard the objections, I now agree that the two-name narrowing should not be taken as a solution while Eshhar is unresolved, and I would present B006 to the vote as a flawed fallback and not a clean one. His point on B020 is useful to me: the pair is clean on the core pathway, but PERK and ATF6 claims remain, and its link to an established intervention is thin. I keep B008 and not B020 as my second alternative only because B008 carries wider reach, not because its attribution is better, and I recognise that a reasonable member could order them the other way.

uncertainties: Whether primary papers and dates show Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide to be distinct from the Habener group's work. Nobody here has verified it.
Whether the committee would accept a different name set if that check is inconclusive, since the supplied ballot offers none for B010 other than Knudsen.
Whether B006 is a usable fallback with Eshhar outside the credited names, and which of B006, B008 or B020 should be the fallback if B010 does not reach four votes.
How much weight accumulating long-term obesity outcome and safety data should carry, which I think affects the drugs more than the discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. My profile records past co-authors Vijay Kuchroo and Sven-Erik Sonesson, and I have no documented involvement with any credited name on the shortlist, including Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen, June, Sadelain and the optogenetics candidates. My own field of autoimmunity and rheumatology is closest to B041 and B021, which I assess on the evidence like any other candidate. No recusal is needed.
